_comment: A scripted AI run (ADR-094). This stands in for a model's judgement and nothing else: every
tool call below is executed against the real engine, through the real registry, inside a real
transaction, on the real main-thread queue. Only the choosing is scripted.
It exists so the whole path can be run and diffed without a credential or a network:
--ai-prompt "make this feel like a cold, foggy night and push the camera in"
The turns follow the behaviour spec section 31 asks for: inspect first, then make a coherent
multi-property change rather than one knob, then verify, then report.

turns.text: Let me see what this scene exposes before changing anything.
Finding the atmosphere and the camera.
A cold night is fog, a cooler sky, a dimmer key and a lower ambient level -- changing one of those alone would look like one thing had been changed.
Now the camera move: a ten-second push, keyed in seconds.
Verifying that the automation bound and nothing is animating a parameter that does not exist.

The scene now reads as a cold night: fog at 0.09 with a shallower height falloff, ambient brightness down to 0.72 and the key light at 0.45, with a little wind so the silhouettes are not static. The camera pushes from 26 metres out to 9 over ten seconds, eased at both ends. All of it is one transaction, so it undoes as one action.
